gaps: No verified paleographic sequence for 他 was obtained. The Xiaoxuetang result resolved to a different headword, and the MOE 佗 entry reports several character-form databases as unavailable.

The sources inspected disagree in how directly they describe the formation: modern character dictionaries analyze 他 as 人/亻 plus phonetic 也, while the quoted Shuowen headword is 佗, analyzed as 人 plus phonetic 它; the Duan note quoted by ZDIC says 佗 changed through clerical writing to 他. This account does not establish whether 也 was an original sound component in 他 or a later analysis/graphic association.

No exact local or external reading for 也 was inspected, so no system-matched historical sound comparison for 也 and 他 is offered. Do not treat the dossier's component assignment alone as proof of phonetic history.
Official Unihan pages for both U+4ED6 and U+4E5F were inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local 他 reading is tā, but it cannot substitute for an inspected Unicode click-through record.

Cited classical passages are transmitted textual attestations, not dated manuscript witnesses. The research did not establish the first attestation date for the “other” sense or the time when third-person 他 became common; the claimed post-Han emergence and displacement timeline remains unverified.

The query for Pulleyblank located bibliographic records but not an inspectable passage supporting the reported third-person pronoun chronology. No evidence here establishes a specific semantic bridge from “other” to third-person reference.
No tracked extract is recommended: the inspected character-specific MOE and ZDIC entries serve the narrow evidentiary purpose, and no verified permission for bulk reuse was found.
No verified paleographic sequence for 他 was obtained. The MOE entry reports its linked early-form references as unavailable; the Xiaoxuetang character-specific page could not be accessed.

The evidence supports a traditional lexicographic account linking 佗 and 他 and distinguishes a later analysis of 他 as 亻+也 from 說文’s 佗 as 人+它. It does not settle whether 也 was an original sound component in 他 or a later graphic/phonetic association.

No exact local or externally verified 也 reading was available for a system-matched comparison. No historical phonetic claim is made for 也. The local Baxter–Sagart rows for 他 and 佗 match, but this is not a row for 也.
The modern tā and tuó readings are only present here as supplied local rows. Official Unicode pages for U+4ED6 and U+4F佗 were inaccessible; the tā reading is not historical sound evidence.

The cited 詩經 and 孟子 lines support transmitted uses of 他 for “other/else,” but do not establish the date of the graph’s first use.
